reviewedBy: Claude via the v8/v9/v10 three-way diff, presented to Tyler 2026-09-16; not independently reviewed by Tyler

base.rationale: The household signs up direct for whatever shows everyone wants to watch, the plan just keeps billing every month unless someone bothers to cancel, and the main worry is paying for a service nobody's really using.

scenarios.label: Household base stack
scenarios.description: A household picks one or two general-purpose streamers for everyday shows and movies.

scenarios.label: Cord-cutting live TV
scenarios.description: They replace cable with a live TV streamer, checking channel lineups, DVR, and streams before committing.

scenarios.label: Tentpole show signup
scenarios.description: They join for a buzzy new season or franchise drop, then plan to cancel after the binge.

scenarios.label: Kids content plan
scenarios.description: Parents add a service for a deep kids library with profiles and parental controls.

cellTexts: [problem_recognition|Household base stack|generic] family of 5, cable bill keeps going up and weeknights we still can't find anything. kids want cartoons, I want movies, my partner wants crime shows. two TVs and a couple tablets. DVR is always full. how do normal people set this up so everyone has something without me babysitting it?

[problem_recognition|Cord-cutting live TV|generic] thinking about cutting the cord but I still need live locals, NFL and college football, a channel guide, and a DVR that won't fill up. it has to work on two TVs and a tablet at the same time, no contract, and not crawl during big games. is that even realistic without a cable box?

[problem_recognition|Tentpole show signup|generic] there's a buzzy sci-fi series I want to binge this weekend. I don't want a long commitment, just that one show, maybe a month tops. what's the sane way to do that?

[problem_recognition|Kids content plan|generic] two kids under 7. I need age-appropriate cartoons and learning shows without random junk popping up, plus downloads for a long flight. can I lock profiles and turn off autoplay somehow?

[category_education|-|generic] ok, so what does a live TV streaming service actually give you compared to cable? do you still get locals, a proper DVR, multiple TVs at once, and how bad is the delay on sports?

[discovery|Household base stack|generic] what's the best streaming setup for a family household? needs good kids library, lots of movies, some international dramas, solid recommendations, 4K on the main TV, and easy profiles.

[discovery|Cord-cutting live TV|generic] best live TV streaming option to replace cable? need locals, NFL/college football and NBA, unlimited or big DVR, at least 3 streams, works on smart TVs, no contract, ideally under 80 a month.
[discovery|Tentpole show signup|generic] best short-term streaming option to watch one buzzy show, month-to-month, easy cancel. ideally 4K on a smart TV and no ads if that's a thing.

[discovery|Kids content plan|generic] best streaming service for kids? looking for strong preschool and early-elementary shows, robust parental controls, profile locks, downloads for travel, and preferably no ads.

[shortlist|Household base stack|generic] can you narrow it to like 3 or 4 streaming services that would cover a family base: big movie catalog, good kids area, some international shows, 4K on the main TV?
[shortlist|Cord-cutting live TV|generic] shortlist 3 solid live TV cord-cutting options that have locals, strong sports coverage, a real DVR, at least 3 simultaneous streams, and no annual contract.
[shortlist|Tentpole show signup|generic] give me 2-3 month-to-month streaming picks that are good for jumping in to watch one hit show and canceling after. easy signup/cancel, 4K if offered.

[shortlist|Kids content plan|generic] top 3 streaming options for kids under 8 with strong parental controls (age filters, profile PIN), lots of ad-free cartoons and educational shows, plus downloads for flights.

[criteria|Household base stack|generic] setting up a base streaming stack for a family of 4. what should I prioritize? content mix, device support, profiles, downloads, ad tiers, price... help me weigh it.

[criteria|Cord-cutting live TV|generic] cutting the cord this fall. for live TV streaming, what specs matter most to compare? thinking channel coverage (locals, sports), DVR rules, stream limits, latency for sports, 4K, device support, price hikes, contracts.

[criteria|Tentpole show signup|generic] there's one big show I want to watch and then bounce. before I sign up, what should I check so I don't get burned? release cadence, free trial fine print, cancellation timing, video quality, region locks?

[criteria|Kids content plan|generic] building a kids-friendly plan for two under 8. what should I look for in a service so it's safe and sane? kid profiles, rating filters, PINs, ad controls, downloads for trips, dubs/subs, screen time tools.

[feature_screening|Cord-cutting live TV|generic] Which live TV streaming options have: local stations in my area; at least 200 hours of cloud DVR that doesn't auto-expire; 3 or more concurrent streams; some sports in 4K; pause/rewind live with start-over? Bonus if picture-in-picture works on phones.

[use_case|Household base stack|generic] household base: two adults (dramas, comedies, some anime), two kids under 10 (animation, nature docs). devices are a smart TV, a streaming stick, and a couple tablets. budget about 40 a month. we'd like 2-3 services max and rotate one slot each month. can you suggest a core stack and a rotation plan?

[use_case|Cord-cutting live TV|generic] Need a clean cable replacement for my parents. Must-have: local news, pro and college sports on weekends, a handful of lifestyle and kids channels. Two TVs and a tablet. They want a simple channel guide, reliable closed captions, and a cloud DVR that can skip ads. Keep it under 80 a month. What service and any extra hardware do they need?

[use_case|Tentpole show signup|generic] I'm only signing up for one show, then cancelling. How do I plan it so I catch the whole season in one month? Things like when episodes drop (weekly vs all at once), whether 4K/HDR costs extra, how long the grace period is after billing, and setting a cancel reminder.

[use_case|Kids content plan|generic] Road trip coming up. Set me up with a kid-safe plan for a 6-year-old: separate profile locked by PIN, max rating around TV-Y7, autoplay off, daily time limit, and downloads only for the tablet with English and Spanish audio. Which services can do that and how to set it up fast?

[social_validation|-|generic] what do people actually love about their favorite streaming service? not specs on a sheet, the identity stuff. is it feeling caught up on the big shows, low ad pain, the app being fast, or the recommendations getting their vibe? give me the social proof angle.

[comparison|Cord-cutting live TV|Disney+] Cutting the cord and want one main service. Netflix vs Disney+: which is the better core if I still need some live news and sports? Compare price, 4K, concurrent streams, downloads, profiles, and parental controls.

[comparison|Cord-cutting live TV|Amazon Prime Video] If I cancel cable, is Netflix or Amazon Prime Video the stronger base for everyday watching? Please compare catalog depth, originals, 4K HDR, offline downloads, simultaneous streams, and how fast movies show up after theaters. I already have an antenna for locals.

[comparison|Cord-cutting live TV|Max] Choosing between Netflix and Max as the main app after dropping cable. Can you compare movie library size, new release windows, any sports plans, 4K upcharges, audio quality, profiles, kid filters, and app stability on Roku?

[comparison|Cord-cutting live TV|Apple TV+] For a light live TV setup, does Netflix or Apple TV+ make more sense as the core, assuming I add a budget live option for sports later? Compare monthly price, catalog breadth, family sharing, 4K availability, downloads, and how often titles rotate out.

[premium_worth|-|generic] Building a family streaming setup on a budget: is paying for the fancy service with the big buzz worth it, or is a cheaper base plus a one month add when a tentpole drops good enough? Kids under 8 in the house.

[objections|Household base stack|generic] Trying to keep our household stack under control. If I add Netflix on top of the two we already pay for, am I just throwing money at shows we won't watch? It feels like it keeps creeping up in price.

[objections|Cord-cutting live TV|generic] Goal is to cut cable to save money, but Netflix keeps raising prices and 4K costs extra. Does keeping Netflix as the core blow the budget compared to using a skinny live TV bundle plus free apps?

[objections|Tentpole show signup|generic] I only want one big series this month on Netflix. I'm worried I'll pay for a month and forget to cancel. How do I do this without it turning into another subscription I barely use?

[objections|Kids content plan|generic] For a kids content plan, is Netflix overpriced for what my 6 and 9 year old actually watch? I don't want to pay premium if they mostly rewatch the same few shows.

[pricing|Household base stack|generic] For a household base stack, what's a sane monthly budget for two paid services plus a rotating slot, and can free apps fill the rest without the ad load getting unbearable?

[pricing|Cord-cutting live TV|generic] Cord cutting math check: what are Netflix's current prices for ad tier, ad free, and 4K, and how does that compare to pairing a low cost live TV bundle with free streamers?

[pricing|Tentpole show signup|generic] Signing up just to binge one flagship series on Netflix: is the ad tier the best value for a single month, or is ad free worth it for the smoother watch? Any minimum terms or extra fees I should watch for?

[pricing|Kids content plan|generic] Kids content budget: across streamers, what gives the best value for under 10s? Is an ad plan fine for cartoons, or do I need ad free to avoid junky ads? Any solid free kids options I can mix in?

[churn_triggers|-|generic] I've had this streaming sub for years but I'm watching less lately and the price crept up again. Feels like my queue is thin. Worth sticking around or should I cancel and come back later?

[alternatives|-|defensive] If I drop Netflix, what services feel closest in mix of buzzy originals, movies, and international series? I care about strong sci-fi, decent kids profiles, and reliable 4K on a living room TV.
[alternatives|-|Disney+] thinking of canceling Disney+. what are good alternatives if we need lots of family-friendly stuff plus a couple big-budget series, with profiles and offline downloads?

[alternatives|-|Amazon Prime Video] I barely use the shopping perks and want to drop Amazon Prime Video. What other streaming options have a big movie library and a few solid originals without tying me to a retail membership?
[alternatives|-|Max] if i cancel Max, where else can I find lots of prestige dramas and docuseries, good 4K, and a decent back catalog?
[alternatives|-|Apple TV+] Apple TV+ feels too thin between tentpole shows. What services hit the same premium-drama vibe but with a deeper library and no ads on the base plan?
[renewal|-|generic] My main streaming plan is up for renewal. Is it smarter to keep it year-round or pause and rotate month to month to save money? We use 4K and watch in two homes.

[problem_resolution|-|generic] On my smart TV the app keeps dropping to 480p even though my internet is fast. Also episodes default to dubbed audio. How do I force 4K, check if my plan includes it, and set English as default?

[expansion|-|generic] Liking the service a lot. Thinking about adding a kids profile, downloading shows for flights, and letting my college kid use it at their dorm. Any limits or extra fees I should watch for?
[ecosystem|-|generic] What gear and apps play nicest with this service? Best streaming box or smart TV setup for smooth 4K HDR, and any watchlist tools that can deep link into it across platforms?
[advocacy|-|generic] I'm trying to convince my roommate not to cancel this and hop between services every month. How do I make the case for keeping it? Practical points only.
